product_one_liner.value: Nanonets provides AI agents that read, validate, route, and post document data to automate document-heavy enterprise workflows such as accounts payable, order management, logistics, and healthcare revenue cycle.
product_one_liner.notes: The about page describes agents that read, validate, route, and post document data and names the enterprise workflows served. Source: https://nanonets.com/about

pricing_page.notes: A public pricing page exists at https://nanonets.com/pricing.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: Roche and Ryanair appear in the company's customer-logo area. Source: http://nanonets.com/agents | named_customers.0: Roche appears in the customer-logo area. Source: http://nanonets.com/agents | named_customers.1: Ryanair appears in the customer-logo area. Source: http://nanonets.com/agents

employee_band.notes: The Y Combinator profile lists a team size of 102, which falls in 101-200. Profile headcount may lag actual staffing. Source: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/nanonets

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The company about page states San Francisco, California, and gives a San Francisco address. Source: https://nanonets.com/about | hq_country: The company lists San Francisco, California, and a San Francisco postal address, placing its headquarters in the United States. Source: https://nanonets.com/about

founded_year.notes: The Y Combinator company profile explicitly lists Founded: 2017. Source: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/nanonets

eng_blog.notes: The research section includes two substantive accounts of building its models: OCR-2 explains synthetic-data training and subsequent fine-tuning, while OCR-3 explains its Mixture-of-Experts architecture and training techniques. OCR-2 is by Nanonets engineer Souvik Mandal; OCR-3 is credited collectively to Nanonets Research, so individual engineering authorship is less explicit for that post. Sources: https://nanonets.com/research, https://nanonets.com/research/nanonets-ocr-2/index.html, http://nanonets.com/research/nanonets-ocr-3, and https://souvik3333.github.io/

public_docs.notes: The public documentation site contains numerous articles covering team management, model setup, API integration, approvals, exports, and other product functions. Source: https://docs.nanonets.com/

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The live company job board lists a Deep Learning Engineer position, with its own application page. Sources: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/nanonets and https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/nanonets/jobs/5372370008

model_provider.notes: Nanonets explicitly identifies OCR-3 as its proprietary extraction model. Source: https://nanonets.com/

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: Nanonets names all four on its homepage; its security policy explicitly confirms SOC 2 compliance and ISO/IEC 27001 certification. HIPAA is qualified as a BAA available for enterprise plans, and GDPR as alignment with EU data-protection laws, rather than independent certifications. Sources: https://nanonets.com/ and https://legal.nanonets.com/security-policy | compliance_certs.0: The security policy explicitly claims SOC 2 compliance and independently attested Type I and Type II reports. Source: https://legal.nanonets.com/security-policy | compliance_certs.1: The security policy explicitly claims ISO/IEC 27001 certification. Source: https://legal.nanonets.com/security-policy | compliance_certs.2: The homepage names HIPAA and says a BAA is available for enterprise plans; this is a qualified compliance claim, not an independent certification claim. Source: https://nanonets.com/ | compliance_certs.3: The homepage names GDPR and claims alignment with EU data-protection laws. Source: https://nanonets.com/
